name: batch
description: Extract content from multiple URLs concurrently.

citations.description: Move link and image URLs out of the markdown into a numbered Links list after each page: `[text](url)` becomes `text[^1]` and a URL used twice on a page keeps one number. Numbers keep counting from page to page. Works with the markdown format

urls.description: List of URLs to extract content from

name: brand
description:
Extract brand identity (colors, fonts, logo, favicon) from a website's HTML and CSS.
Automatically falls back to the webclaw cloud API when bot protection is detected.

url.description: URL to extract brand identity from

name: crawl
description: Crawl a website starting from a seed URL, following links breadth-first up to a configurable depth and page limit. With `query`, the links most likely to answer it are followed first and pages come back best match first, each cut to the parts that answer it.

block.description: When rendering, skip these resources so pages download less: a comma list of "images", "fonts" and "media", or "none"

chunk.description: Return chunks for retrieval instead: one JSON object with the crawl counts (total, ok, errors, skipped_by_robots), the failed pages with their error, and the chunks of every page, each under about this many tokens with its page url, index, heading_path, tokens and markdown text

chunk_overlap.description: With `chunk`, start each chunk with up to this many tokens from the end of the one before (at most half the chunk size)

citations.description: Move link and image URLs out of the markdown into a numbered Links list at the end: `[text](url)` becomes `text[^1]` and a URL used twice keeps one number. Works with the markdown format, not with chunk

ignore_robots.description: Crawl URLs that robots.txt disallows (default: false)

max_pages.description: Maximum number of pages to crawl (default: 50)

query.description: A question, up to 1000 characters: follow the links most likely to answer it first, keep only the parts of each page that answer it, and list pages best match first

stop_when_answered.description: With `query`, stop once a page rated at least 0.8 has been found and the next 8 pages rated no higher, instead of always crawling up to max_pages

url.description: Seed URL to start crawling from

use_sitemap.description: Seed the frontier from sitemap discovery before crawling

name: diff
description:
Compare the current content of a URL against a previous extraction snapshot, showing what changed.
Automatically falls back to the webclaw cloud API when bot protection is detected.

previous_snapshot.description: Previous extraction snapshot as a JSON string (ExtractionResult)

url.description: URL to fetch current content from

name: extract
description:
Extract structured data from a web page using an LLM. Provide either a JSON schema or a natural language prompt.
Falls back to the webclaw cloud API when no local LLM is available or bot protection is detected.

prompt.description: Natural language prompt describing what to extract

schema.description: JSON schema describing the structure to extract

url.description: URL to fetch and extract structured data from

name: list_extractors
description:
List every vertical extractor the server knows about. Returns a
JSON array of `{name, label, description, url_patterns}` entries.
Call this to discover what verticals are available before using
`vertical_scrape`.

name: map
description: Discover URLs from a website's sitemaps (robots.txt + sitemap.xml), adding the links a short crawl of the site finds when the sitemaps list fewer than 200 URLs, and with `source` "sitemap,cc" or "cc" from the public Common Crawl index too, which also finds pages no sitemap lists.

limit.description: Return at most this many URLs

query.description: A question, up to 1000 characters: list URLs best match first by the words in their paths

source.description: Where to look, comma-separated: "sitemap" (default, plus a short crawl of the site when the sitemaps list fewer than 200 URLs) and "cc", the public Common Crawl index of the HTML pages it captured on the site, e.g. "sitemap,cc". The index is often slow: a lookup takes 10 to 60 seconds and gives up after 2 minutes, keeping the URLs read until then

url.description: Base URL to discover sitemaps from (e.g. `<https://example.com>`)

name: research
description:
Run a deep research investigation on a topic or question. Requires WEBCLAW_API_KEY.
Saves full result to ~/.webclaw/research/ and returns the file path + key findings.
Checks cache first — same query returns the cached result without spending credits.

deep.description: Enable deep research mode for more thorough investigation (default: false)

query.description: Research query or question to investigate

topic.description: Topic hint to guide research focus (e.g. "technology", "finance", "science")

name: scrape
description:
Scrape a single URL and extract its content as markdown, LLM-optimized text, plain text, or full JSON.
Pages whose content needs JavaScript are rendered in a local Chrome when this server has browser support; otherwise, and on bot protection, it falls back to the webclaw cloud API when WEBCLAW_API_KEY is set.
A server without browser support sends `render` "always", `wait_for`, `solve` and `actions` to the hosted API when WEBCLAW_API_KEY is set, and without a key returns a page that needs JavaScript with a notice saying so.
With `actions`, in the hosted API's format, the page is rendered and the steps (click, type, press, scroll, wait, waitForSelector, executeJavascript) run before it is read, for infinite scroll, "load more" buttons, tabs and forms.
With `capture_network`, the page is rendered in the local Chrome and the XHR and fetch responses it loaded (the JSON a single-page app gets from its API) come back after the content.

actions.description: Steps to run in the browser once the page has loaded, before it is read. The page is always rendered when this is set. Each step is an object with a "type", as in the hosted API: {"type": "click", "selector": CSS} with optionally "nth": index from 0, "all": true, or "repeat": N to keep clicking a "load more" button until it is gone; {"type": "type", "selector": CSS, "value": "..."}; {"type": "press", "key": "Enter"}; {"type": "scroll"} to the end, optionally with "direction": "down" or "up", "amount": pixels, "selector" for a scrollable element, and "repeat": N to keep scrolling until the page stops growing; {"type": "wait", "milliseconds": 1000}; {"type": "waitForSelector", "selector": CSS, "timeout": 10000}; {"type": "executeJavascript", "code": "JavaScript expression"} whose value is returned as js_results. A failing step fails the call and its number is in the error. A server without browser support runs the steps through the hosted API when WEBCLAW_API_KEY is set, without nth, all, repeat or a scroll selector

block.description: When rendering, skip these resources so pages download less: a comma list of "images", "fonts" and "media", or "none". Pages rendered through the hosted API ignore it

capture_credentials.description: With `capture_network`, also keep request headers that carry credentials, such as Authorization or API keys (default: false)

capture_network.description: Render the page in the local Chrome (needs a server with browser support) and also return the responses it loaded whose URL matches this regular expression, "" for all: url, method, status, resource_type, mime_type, request_headers and the body of text responses (at most 100 responses, each body cut to 100 KB and all bodies together to 1 MB). Single-page apps load their data as JSON this way, often cleaner than the page. Runs after `actions`, so it also catches what they trigger

capture_types.description: With `capture_network`, the resource types to keep: a comma list such as "xhr,fetch" (the default), "document", "script", or "all"

chunk.description: Return the page as a JSON array of chunks for retrieval instead, each under about this many tokens, with url, index, heading_path, tokens and markdown text. Paragraphs, lists, tables and code blocks stay whole

chunk_overlap.description: With `chunk`, start each chunk with up to this many tokens from the end of the one before (at most half the chunk size)

citations.description: Move link and image URLs out of the markdown into a numbered Links list at the end: `[text](url)` becomes `text[^1]` and a URL used twice keeps one number. Works with the markdown format and the markdown inside "json", not with chunk

cookies.description: Cookies to send with the request (e.g. ["name=value", "session=abc123"]). When the server keeps a browser profile (WEBCLAW_BROWSER_PROFILE), they are saved in it for this URL and sent on later calls too

exclude_selectors.description: CSS selectors to exclude from output

include_selectors.description: CSS selectors to include (only extract matching elements)

only_main_content.description: If true, extract only the main content (article/main element)

query.description: A question: keep only the parts of the page that answer it, under their headings

render.description: JavaScript rendering: "auto" (default) renders pages whose content needs it, "always" renders every page that runs scripts, "never" skips it. Pages render in a local Chrome when this server has browser support, otherwise through the hosted API when WEBCLAW_API_KEY is set

solve.description: Get past a Cloudflare challenge page in the local Chrome: wait for it to clear or click its checkbox, then read the page it leads to. A Turnstile checkbox in any page that gets rendered is clicked too. A server without browser support reads the page through the hosted API instead when WEBCLAW_API_KEY is set

wait_for.description: When rendering, also wait until an element matching this CSS selector exists

name: screenshot
description: Capture a web page after its scripts ran, as an image, a PDF or an MHTML archive, in the local Chrome when this server has browser support. A server without it captures PNG images through the hosted API when WEBCLAW_API_KEY is set. Images (PNG, or JPEG with `format`) show the 1280x720 viewport, or the whole page with `full_page`. With format "pdf" the whole page is printed to a Letter or A4 PDF and returned as an application/pdf resource of up to 10 MiB. With format "mhtml" the page is saved with the images, styles and frames it loaded as one file a browser opens offline, returned as a multipart/related resource of up to 10 MiB. Also returns the final URL, and with `actions` the values of their executeJavascript steps.

actions.description: Steps to run in the browser once the page has loaded, before it is captured. Each step is an object with a "type", as in the hosted API: {"type": "click", "selector": CSS} with optionally "nth": index from 0, "all": true, or "repeat": N to keep clicking a "load more" button until it is gone; {"type": "type", "selector": CSS, "value": "..."}; {"type": "press", "key": "Enter"}; {"type": "scroll"} to the end, optionally with "direction": "down" or "up", "amount": pixels, "selector" for a scrollable element, and "repeat": N to keep scrolling until the page stops growing; {"type": "wait", "milliseconds": 1000}; {"type": "waitForSelector", "selector": CSS, "timeout": 10000}; {"type": "executeJavascript", "code": "JavaScript expression"} whose value is returned as js_results. A failing step fails the call and its number is in the error. A server without browser support runs the steps through the hosted API when WEBCLAW_API_KEY is set, without nth, all, repeat or a scroll selector

format.description: "png" (default) or "jpeg", which is smaller, for an image, "pdf" to print the whole page to a PDF instead, or "mhtml" to save it as one MHTML file with its images and styles, which a browser opens offline

full_page.description: For images, capture the whole scrollable page instead of the 1280x720 viewport (default: false). A PDF or MHTML file always holds the whole page

print_background.description: With format "pdf": keep background colors and images, which browsers leave out when printing (default: false)

wait_for.description: Also wait until an element matching this CSS selector exists before capturing

name: search
description:
Search the web for a query and return structured results.
Resolves the backend in priority order:
1. `SERPER_API_KEY` set → local Serper.dev search with the user's
own key (no hosted API needed). Supports `country`, `lang`, and
`scrape` (fetch + extract each result page).
2. else `WEBCLAW_API_KEY` set → the hosted webclaw search API.
3. else → an error explaining both options.

country.description:
Country code for localization (e.g. "us", "gb", "it").
Only used by the local Serper path (SERPER_API_KEY).

lang.description:
Language code for localization (e.g. "en", "it").
Only used by the local Serper path (SERPER_API_KEY).

num_results.description: Number of results to return (default: 5, max: 10)

scrape.description:
When true, fetch + extract each result page and include its
markdown. Only used by the local Serper path (SERPER_API_KEY).

name: select
description:
Pick values out of a web page with a CSS selector or an XPath 1.0 expression and return them as a JSON array: text by default, or an attribute or HTML with a "::attr(NAME)" or "::html" ending (CSS), or "@attr" (XPath). With `fields`, return one JSON object per match, each field a selector run inside that match. With `tables`, return the page's data tables as headers and rows. With `text` or `regex`, find the elements holding that text instead. With `similar`, take the first element picked as an example and return every element like it, with a CSS selector that picks them all.
Pages whose content needs JavaScript are rendered first when this server has browser support.

case_sensitive.description: With `text` or `regex`, match letter case (default: false)

exact.description: With `text`, match the whole text instead of a part (default: false)

fields.description: Return one object per match instead: field name to a selector run inside that match, e.g. {"title": "h3 a::attr(title)", "price": ".price_color"}, or with `xpath` an expression relative to the match, e.g. {"title": ".//h3/a/@title"}. With `similar` the fields are CSS

regex.description: Like `text` with a regular expression, e.g. "^£\d+\.\d\d$"

selector.description: CSS selector, optionally ending in "::text" (default), "::attr(NAME)" or "::html", e.g. "h3 a::attr(href)". Give exactly one of `selector`, `xpath`, `tables`, `text` and `regex`

similar.description: Use the first element `selector`, `xpath`, `text` or `regex` picks as an example and return every element like it with one CSS selector that picks them all: {"selector", "matches"}, or with `fields` {"selector", "records"} (default: false)

tables.description: Return the page's data tables instead, each as {"caption", "headers", "rows"} with rows of cell text; layout tables are skipped

text.description: Find the deepest elements whose visible text contains this, any case. Returns [{"selector", "text"}], each selector picking its element alone

xpath.description: XPath 1.0 expression instead of a CSS selector, e.g. "//h3/a/@title". Elements and text give their text, attributes their value

name: summarize
description:
Summarize the content of a web page using an LLM.
Falls back to the webclaw cloud API when no local LLM is available or bot protection is detected.

max_sentences.description: Number of sentences in the summary (default: 3)

name: vertical_scrape
description:
Run a vertical extractor by name and return typed JSON specific
to the target site (title, price, rating, author, etc.), not
generic markdown. Use `list_extractors` to discover available
names. Example names: `reddit`, `github_repo`, `trustpilot_reviews`,
`youtube_video`, `shopify_product`, `pypi`, `npm`, `arxiv`.
Antibot-gated verticals (amazon_product, ebay_listing,
etsy_listing, trustpilot_reviews) will automatically escalate to
the webclaw cloud API when local fetch hits bot protection,
provided `WEBCLAW_API_KEY` is set.

name.description:
Name of the vertical extractor. Call `list_extractors` to see all
available names. Examples: "reddit", "github_repo", "pypi",
"trustpilot_reviews", "youtube_video", "shopify_product".

url.description:
URL to extract. Must match the URL patterns the extractor claims;
otherwise the tool returns a clear "URL mismatch" error.
